text:
alex: Quick proposal for low-impact nsys sampling in prod. TL;DR: enable sampling-only nsys traces at 1% of requests, 200ms capture windows, persist minimal event lists. Full captures only on canary or explicit debug runs. Thoughts?

maria: +1 to sampling but we should tie sample rate to KV cache hit ratio and request size. small seq len requests hurt SNR. also we need PII redaction in traces.

sam: can you drop expected overhead numbers? ops will freak without estimates.

alex: rough numbers from our staging runs: 1% sampling ~= +0.5% p50 latency, p95 ~ +1.2%. full nsys captures were brutal: ~15-20% latency inflation and large IO. probe overhead (when active) ~8-12ms per kernel-event in hot paths.

jin: i ran a 4h A/B on staging yesterday: sampling=1% => overall CPU up ~3%, network IO for traces ~60MB/s at peak, disk writes ~10MB/s since we aggregate before flush. Full capture was ~18% CPU and 200-300MB/s. logs: 
```
[staging-run] sampling=0.01 window_ms=200 traces-emitted=472 avg-emit-size=128KB
[staging-run] full-capture=disabled
```

tyler: we need explicit guardrails:
- per-host daily trace quota (eg 500 traces/day)
- backoff if latency > threshold (eg p95 > baseline * 1.15)
- disable on Dedicated customers by default
- redact payload fields: prompt, user_id, tokens -> hash

alex: agree on quotas and backoff. propose config snippet for rollout:
```
profiler:
  mode: sampling
  sample_rate: 0.01
  window_ms: 200
  per_host_quota: 500
  backoff_latency_multiplier: 1.15
  redact: ["user_id", "prompt"]
```

maria: also add dynamic-scaling: if CPU or GPU utilization < 30% and qps > threshold then increase sample_rate to 2% for 15m to catch anomalies. revert after.

sam: question: how do we avoid skewed samples (only heavy requests)? need fair sampling across endpoints. maybe reservoir sampling keyed by route.

jin: implemented simple stratified sampler in staging: 
```
# pseudo
if route not seen in last 10min: force-sample(route)  # ensure coverage
else: sample_random(rate)
```
it caught a kernel miscompile on a rare route.

alex: good find. For rollout plan: canary in eu-west for 48h, collect perf metrics and safety signals, then global 7-day ramp. We'll only emit flamegraphs to internal bucket and TTL them 7d.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary deployment scheduled to eng-runtime-staging at 2026-06-04T03:00Z if approved.

tyler: minor nit: ensure telemetry log level for sampled traces is DEBUG only, and do not escalate logs to user-facing error channels.

maria: volunteer to run the first canary and dump metrics to the perf dashboard. :thumbsup:

sam: i'll add an evaluation probe to flag regressions if p95 increases by >5% for 2 consecutive windows. :eyes:

alex: awesome. i'll author an RFC with config + dashboards + checklist. tagging @maria @sam to help with runbook. thanks everyone.
